sanskrit: prāptakālaṃ subalavan niścitya bahudhā hi me tatraiva pāṇḍaveyasya bhīmasenasya dhanvinaḥ gamanaṃ rocate mahyaṃ yatra yātau mahārathau
english: Having weighed the matter many times over and judged it most fitting to the hour, it seems best to me that Bhīmasena the bowman, the son of Pāṇḍu, should go to that very place where the two great car-warriors have gone.

sanskrit: na cāpy asahyaṃ bhīmasya vidyate bhuvi kiṃ cana śakto hy eṣa raṇe yattān pṛthivyāṃ sarvadhanvinaḥ svabāhubalam āsthāya prativyūhitum añjasā
english: There is nothing on earth that Bhīma cannot endure; relying on the strength of his own arms, he is able with ease to hold at bay in battle all the bowmen of the earth, however resolute they stand.

sanskrit: yasya bāhubalaṃ sarve samāśritya mahātmanaḥ vanavāsān nivṛttāḥ sma na ca yuddheṣu nirjitāḥ
english: Leaning upon the might of that great-souled one's arms, we all returned from our dwelling in the forest, and in our battles we were never overcome.

sanskrit: ito gate bhīmasene sātvataṃ prati pāṇḍave sanāthau bhavitārau hi yudhi sātvataphalgunau
english: If Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava goes from here toward the Sātvata, then in the fight the Sātvata and Phalguna will both have a protector at hand.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ tv aśocanīyau tau raṇe sātvataphalgunau rakṣitau vāsudevena svayaṃ cāstraviśāradau
english: To be sure, the Sātvata and Phalguna need not be grieved over in battle, for they are guarded by Vāsudeva himself, and are themselves masters of every weapon.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ tu mayā kāryam ātmanaḥ śokanāśanam tasmād bhīmaṃ niyokṣyāmi sātvatasya padānugam tataḥ pratikṛtaṃ manye vidhānaṃ sātyakiṃ prati
english: Yet I must surely do something to dispel my own grief; therefore I shall appoint Bhīma to follow upon the Sātvata's track. By this I think the measure on behalf of Sātyaki will be fulfilled.

sanskrit: evaṃ niścitya manasā dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ yantāram abravīd rājan bhīmaṃ prati nayasva mām
english: Having resolved thus in his mind, O king, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Dharma said to his charioteer, "Drive me toward Bhīma."

sanskrit: dharmarājavacaḥ śrutvā sārathir hayakovidaḥ rathaṃ hemapariṣkāraṃ bhīmāntikam upānayat
english: Hearing the word of the Dharma-king, the charioteer skilled with horses brought the gold-adorned car near to Bhīma.

sanskrit: bhīmasenam anuprāpya prāptakālam anusmaran kaśmalaṃ prāviśad rājā bahu tatra samādiśan
english: Having reached Bhīmasena, and calling to mind what the hour demanded, the king sank into despondency even as he gave him many commands.

sanskrit: yaḥ sadevān sagandharvān daityāṃś caikaratho 'jayat tasya lakṣma na paśyāmi bhīmasenānujasya te
english: "He who, alone upon his car, conquered the gods together with the Gandharvas and the Daityas — of him, your younger brother Bhīmasena, I see no sign."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd dharmarājaṃ bhīmasenas tathāgatam naivādrākṣaṃ na cāśrauṣaṃ tava kaśmalam īdṛśam
english: Then Bhīmasena said to the Dharma-king, who had come to him in such a state, "Never have I seen nor heard such despondency in you."

sanskrit: purā hi duḥkhadīrṇānāṃ bhavān gatir abhūd dhi naḥ uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha rājendra śādhi kiṃ karavāṇi te
english: "In days past, when we were torn by sorrows, it was you who were our refuge. Rise up, rise up, lord of kings; command me — what shall I do for you?"

sanskrit: na hy asādhyam akāryaṃ vā vidyate mama mānada ājñāpaya kuruśreṣṭha mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: "There is nothing impossible for me, nor anything I will not do, O giver of honor. Give the order, best of the Kurus, and do not set your mind upon grief."

sanskrit: tam abravīd aśrupūrṇaḥ kṛṣṇasarpa iva śvasan bhīmasenam idaṃ vākyaṃ pramlānavadano nṛpaḥ
english: To him the king, his eyes brimming with tears, hissing like a black serpent, his face withered, spoke these words to Bhīmasena:

sanskrit: yathā śaṅkhasya nirghoṣaḥ pāñcajanyasya śrūyate prerito vāsudevena saṃrabdhena yaśasvinā nūnam adya hataḥ śete tava bhrātā dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: "As the blast of the conch Pāñcajanya is heard, blown by the glorious Vāsudeva in his fury, surely your brother Dhanaṃjaya lies slain this day."

sanskrit: tasmin vinihate nūnaṃ yudhyate 'sau janārdanaḥ yasya sattvavato vīryam upajīvanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: "He being struck down, Janārdana himself surely fights on now — he, by whose valor, mighty in spirit, the Pāṇḍavas live."

sanskrit: yaṃ bhayeṣv abhigacchanti sahasrākṣam ivāmarāḥ sa śūraḥ saindhavaprepsur anvayād bhāratīṃ camūm
english: "To whom in times of peril we resort as the immortals resort to the thousand-eyed one — that hero, seeking the ruler of the Sindhus, followed after the Bhārata host."

sanskrit: tasya vai gamanaṃ vidmo bhīma nāvartanaṃ punaḥ śyāmo yuvā guḍākeśo darśanīyo mahābhujaḥ
english: "Of his going, Bhīma, we know; of his return we have no word — that dark, youthful one, Guḍākeśa, fair to look upon, mighty-armed,"

sanskrit: vyūḍhorasko mahāskandho mattadviradavikramaḥ cakoranetras tāmrākṣo dviṣatām aghavardhanaḥ
english: "broad-chested, great-shouldered, with the stride of a rutting elephant, eyes like the cakora bird, copper-hued of eye, swelling the woes of his foes."

sanskrit: tad idaṃ mama bhadraṃ te śokasthānam ariṃdama arjunārthaṃ mahābāho sātvatasya ca kāraṇāt
english: "This, then — blessings upon you, crusher of foes — is the ground of my grief: for Arjuna's sake, O mighty-armed one, and on the Sātvata's account."

sanskrit: vardhate haviṣevāgnir idhyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ tasya lakṣma na paśyāmi tena vindāmi kaśmalam
english: "It grows as fire kindled with oblation grows, blazing up again and again. Of him I see no sign, and so I am overcome with despondency."

sanskrit: taṃ viddhi puruṣavyāghraṃ sātvataṃ ca mahāratham sa taṃ mahārathaṃ paścād anuyātas tavānujam tam apaśyan mahābāhum ahaṃ vindāmi kaśmalam
english: "Know too that tiger among men, the Sātvata, the great car-warrior: he followed afterward upon the track of that great car-warrior, your younger brother. Not seeing that mighty-armed one, I am sunk in despondency."

sanskrit: tasmāt kṛṣṇo raṇe nūnaṃ yudhyate yuddhakovidaḥ yasya vīryavato vīryam upajīvanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: "Therefore Kṛṣṇa, skilled in war, surely now fights on in battle — he by whose valor, mighty in might, the Pāṇḍavas live."

sanskrit: sa tatra gaccha kaunteya yatra yāto dhanaṃjayaḥ sātyakiś ca mahāvīryaḥ kartavyaṃ yadi manyase vacanaṃ mama dharmajña jyeṣṭho bhrātā bhavāmi te
english: "Go you there, son of Kuntī, where Dhanaṃjaya has gone, and Sātyaki of great valor — if you hold my word fit to be obeyed, O knower of dharma, for I am your eldest brother."

sanskrit: na te 'rjunas tathā jñeyo jñātavyaḥ sātyakir yathā cikīrṣur matpriyaṃ pārtha prayātaḥ savyasācinaḥ padavīṃ durgamāṃ ghorām agamyām akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: "You need not be so concerned for Arjuna as you must be for Sātyaki, O Pārtha, who, wishing to do me a kindness, set out along Savyasācin's path — hard to traverse, terrible, impassable to the unschooled in soul."

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca brahmeśānendravaruṇān avahad yaḥ purā rathaḥ tam āsthāya gatau kṛṣṇau na tayor vidyate bhayam
english: Bhīmasena said: "The car that of old bore Brahmā, Īśāna, Indra, and Varuṇa — mounted upon that, the two Kṛṣṇas have gone; for them there is no fear."

sanskrit: ājñāṃ tu śirasā bibhrad eṣa gacchāmi mā śucaḥ sametya tān naravyāghrāṃs tava dāsyāmi saṃvidam
english: "Yet bearing your command upon my head, here I go — grieve not. Having met those tigers among men, I shall send you tidings."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca etāvad uktvā prayayau paridāya yudhiṣṭhiram dhṛṣṭadyumnāya balavān suhṛdbhyaś ca punaḥ punaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ cedam āha bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Having spoken thus much, the mighty one set forth, entrusting Yudhiṣṭhira again and again to Dhṛṣṭadyumna and to his friends; and Bhīmasena of great strength said this to Dhṛṣṭadyumna:

sanskrit: viditaṃ te mahābāho yathā droṇo mahārathaḥ grahaṇe dharmarājasya sarvopāyena vartate
english: "You know, mighty-armed one, how Droṇa the great car-warrior bends every means toward the capture of the Dharma-king."

sanskrit: na ca me gamane kṛtyaṃ tādṛk pārṣata vidyate yādṛśaṃ rakṣaṇe rājñaḥ kāryam ātyayikaṃ hi naḥ
english: "No duty in my going, O son of Pṛṣata, weighs upon me as does the guarding of the king; for that is our most pressing task."

sanskrit: evam ukto 'smi pārthena prativaktuṃ sma notsahe prayāsye tatra yatrāsau mumūrṣuḥ saindhavaḥ sthitaḥ dharmarājasya vacane sthātavyam aviśaṅkayā
english: "Thus has Pārtha bidden me, and I cannot gainsay it; I shall go there where the Saindhava, doomed to die, has taken his stand. By the word of the Dharma-king one must stand without misgiving."

sanskrit: so 'dya yatto raṇe pārthaṃ parirakṣa yudhiṣṭhiram etad dhi sarvakāryāṇāṃ paramaṃ kṛtyam āhave
english: "So this day, intent in battle, guard Pārtha Yudhiṣṭhira; for this is, of all our charges, the highest task in the fray."

sanskrit: tam abravīn mahārāja dhṛṣṭadyumno vṛkodaram īpsitena mahābāho gaccha pārthāvicārayan
english: To him, O great king, Dhṛṣṭadyumna said to Vṛkodara, "Go, mighty-armed one, as you desire, untroubled in heart, O Pārtha."

sanskrit: nāhatvā samare droṇo dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ kathaṃ cana nigrahaṃ dharmarājasya prakariṣyati saṃyuge
english: "Not until in battle he has slain Dhṛṣṭadyumna will Droṇa ever in the encounter lay hold of the Dharma-king."

sanskrit: tato nikṣipya rājānaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnāya pāṇḍavaḥ abhivādya guruṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ prayayau yatra phalgunaḥ
english: Then the Pāṇḍava, committing the king to Dhṛṣṭadyumna and saluting his elder, his guide, set forth to where Phalguna was.

sanskrit: pariṣvaktas tu kaunteyo dharmarājena bhārata āghrātaś ca tathā mūrdhni śrāvitaś cāśiṣaḥ śubhāḥ
english: The son of Kuntī, O Bhārata, was embraced by the Dharma-king, kissed upon the head, and given fair blessings to hear.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno mahābāhuḥ kavacī śubhakuṇḍalī sāṅgadaḥ satanutrāṇaḥ saśarī rathināṃ varaḥ
english: Bhīmasena, the mighty-armed, mailed, with bright earrings, with armlets, with cuirass, with arrows — the foremost of car-warriors —

sanskrit: tasya kārṣṇāyasaṃ varma hemacitraṃ maharddhimat vibabhau parvataśliṣṭaḥ savidyud iva toyadaḥ
english: his armor of black iron, figured with gold and richly wrought, shone like a lightning-laced rain-cloud clinging to a mountain.

sanskrit: pītaraktāsitasitair vāsobhiś ca suveṣṭitaḥ kaṇṭhatrāṇena ca babhau sendrāyudha ivāmbudaḥ
english: Well-wrapped in cloths of yellow, red, black, and white, and with his throat-guard, he gleamed like a cloud spanned by Indra's bow.

sanskrit: prayāte bhīmasene tu tava sainyaṃ yuyutsayā pāñcajanyaravo ghoraḥ punar āsīd viśāṃ pate
english: When Bhīmasena had set forth eager for battle against your army, again, O lord of peoples, there rose the terrible blast of the Pāñcajanya.

sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā ninadaṃ ghoraṃ trailokyatrāsanaṃ mahat punar bhīmaṃ mahābāhur dharmaputro 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Hearing that terrible roar, vast and terrifying to the three worlds, the mighty-armed son of Dharma again spoke to Bhīma:

sanskrit: eṣa vṛṣṇipravīreṇa dhmātaḥ salilajo bhṛśam pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣaṃ ca vinādayati śaṅkharāṭ
english: "This king of conches, the water-born, blown hard by the Vṛṣṇi hero, makes earth and the mid-air resound."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ vyasanam āpanne sumahat savyasācini kurubhir yudhyate sārdhaṃ sarvaiś cakragadādharaḥ
english: "Surely, some great calamity having befallen Savyasācin, the bearer of discus and mace fights now against all the Kurus."

sanskrit: nūnam āryā mahat kuntī pāpam adya nidarśanam draupadī ca subhadrā ca paśyanti saha bandhubhiḥ
english: "Surely the noble Kuntī, and Draupadī, and Subhadrā behold this day, together with their kinsfolk, the showing of a great evil."

sanskrit: sa bhīmas tvarayā yukto yāhi yatra dhanaṃjayaḥ muhyantīva hi me sarvā dhanaṃjayadidṛkṣayā diśaḥ sapradiśaḥ pārtha sātvatasya ca kāraṇāt
english: "So, Bhīma, set with haste, go where Dhanaṃjaya is; for all the quarters and their sub-quarters seem to swim before me, O Pārtha, out of longing to see Dhanaṃjaya, and on the Sātvata's account."

sanskrit: gaccha gaccheti ca punar bhīmasenam abhāṣata bhṛśaṃ sa prahito bhrātrā bhrātā bhrātuḥ priyaṃkaraḥ āhatya dundubhiṃ bhīmaḥ śaṅkhaṃ pradhmāya cāsakṛt
english: "Go, go," he said again to Bhīmasena. Urged on hard by his brother, that brother who did his brother's pleasure, Bhīma struck the war-drum and blew the conch again and again,

sanskrit: vinadya siṃhanādaṃ ca jyāṃ vikarṣan punaḥ punaḥ darśayan ghoram ātmānam amitrān sahasābhyayāt
english: and roaring his lion's roar, drawing the bowstring again and again, showing forth his terrible self, he rushed suddenly upon the foe.

sanskrit: tam ūhur javanā dāntā vikurvāṇā hayottamāḥ viśokenābhisaṃyattā manomārutaraṃhasaḥ
english: Him the swift, well-broken, prancing best of horses bore on, harnessed by Viśoka, fleet as mind and wind.

sanskrit: ārujan virujan pārtho jyāṃ vikarṣaṃś ca pāṇinā so 'vakarṣan vikarṣaṃś ca senāgraṃ samaloḍayat
english: Shattering and crushing, drawing the bowstring with his hand, Pārtha, dragging it down and drawing it back, churned up the vanguard of the host.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntaṃ mahābāhuṃ pāñcālāḥ sahasomakāḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nuyayuḥ śūrā maghavantam ivāmarāḥ
english: As he went on, that mighty-armed one, the Pāñcālas together with the Somakas, heroes, followed behind him as the immortals follow Maghavan.

sanskrit: taṃ sasenā mahārāja sodaryāḥ paryavārayan duḥśalaś citrasenaś ca kuṇḍabhedī viviṃśatiḥ
english: Him, O great king, your sons born of one womb hemmed in with their troops — Duḥśalā and Citrasena and Kuṇḍabhedī and Viviṃśati,

sanskrit: durmukho duḥsahaś caiva vikarṇaś ca śalas tathā vindānuvindau sumukho dīrghabāhuḥ sudarśanaḥ
english: Durmukha and Duḥsaha, and Vikarṇa, and Śala too, Vinda and Anuvinda, Sumukha, Dīrghabāhu, Sudarśana,

sanskrit: vṛndārakaḥ suhastaś ca suṣeṇo dīrghalocanaḥ abhayo raudrakarmā ca suvarmā durvimocanaḥ
english: Vṛndāraka and Suhasta, Suṣeṇa, Dīrghalocana, Abhaya and Raudrakarman, Suvarman and Durvimocana —

sanskrit: vividhai rathināṃ śreṣṭhāḥ saha sainyaiḥ sahānugaiḥ saṃyattāḥ samare śūrā bhīmasenam upādravan
english: these foremost of car-warriors, with their varied troops and their followers, girt for battle, the heroes, rushed upon Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tān samīkṣya tu kaunteyo bhīmasenaḥ parākramī abhyavartata vegena siṃhaḥ kṣudramṛgān iva
english: Beholding them, the son of Kuntī, valiant Bhīmasena, turned upon them with speed, as a lion upon lesser beasts.

sanskrit: te mahāstrāṇi divyāni tatra vīrā adarśayan vārayantaḥ śarair bhīmaṃ meghāḥ sūryam ivoditam
english: There those heroes displayed great celestial weapons, holding off Bhīma with their arrows as clouds hold off the risen sun.

sanskrit: sa tān atītya vegena droṇānīkam upādravat agrataś ca gajānīkaṃ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: Passing them by with speed, he rushed upon Droṇa's division, and the elephant-host before him he overwhelmed with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: so 'cireṇaiva kālena tad gajānīkam āśugaiḥ diśaḥ sarvāḥ samabhyasya vyadhamat pavanātmajaḥ
english: In but a little while the son of the Wind, sweeping his swift shafts in every direction, scattered that elephant-host.

sanskrit: trāsitāḥ śarabhasyeva garjitena vane mṛgāḥ prādravan dviradāḥ sarve nadanto bhairavān ravān
english: As beasts in the forest are frightened by the roar of the śarabha, all those elephants fled, bellowing dreadful cries.

sanskrit: punaś cātītya vegena droṇānīkam upādravat tam avārayad ācāryo velevodvṛttam arṇavam
english: And again, passing on with speed, he rushed upon Droṇa's division; the preceptor held him back as the shore holds back the swollen sea.

sanskrit: lalāṭe 'tāḍayac cainaṃ nārācena smayann iva ūrdhvaraśmir ivādityo vibabhau tatra pāṇḍavaḥ
english: He struck him on the forehead with an iron shaft, smiling as it were; and the Pāṇḍava shone there like the sun with rays upraised.

sanskrit: sa manyamānas tv ācāryo mamāyaṃ phalguno yathā bhīmaḥ kariṣyate pūjām ity uvāca vṛkodaram
english: And the preceptor, supposing that Bhīma would do him honor as Phalguna would, said to Vṛkodara:

sanskrit: bhīmasena na te śakyaṃ praveṣṭum arivāhinīm mām anirjitya samare śatrumadhye mahābala
english: "Bhīmasena, you cannot pierce into the enemy's host without first conquering me in battle, O mighty one, here amid the foes."

sanskrit: yadi te so 'nujaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ praviṣṭo 'numate mama anīkaṃ na tu śakyaṃ bhoḥ praveṣṭum iha vai tvayā
english: "If that younger brother of yours, and Kṛṣṇa, entered with my leave, yet this array, sir, cannot be entered here by you."

sanskrit: atha bhīmas tu tac chrutvā guror vākyam apetabhīḥ kruddhaḥ provāca vai droṇaṃ raktatāmrekṣaṇaḥ śvasan
english: Then Bhīma, fearless, hearing that word of the teacher, wrathful, his eyes red as copper, hissing with breath, spoke to Droṇa:

sanskrit: tavārjuno nānumate brahmabandho raṇājiram praviṣṭaḥ sa hi durdharṣaḥ śakrasyāpi viśed balam
english: "Not by your leave, O wretch of a brahmin, did Arjuna enter the field of war; for he, unassailable, could pierce even the host of Śakra."

sanskrit: yena vai paramāṃ pūjāṃ kurvatā mānito hy asi nārjuno 'haṃ ghṛṇī droṇa bhīmaseno 'smi te ripuḥ
english: "By him, doing you the highest honor, you have indeed been honored; but I am no Arjuna full of compassion, Droṇa — I am Bhīmasena, your enemy."

sanskrit: pitā nas tvaṃ gurur bandhus tathā putrā hi te vayam iti manyāmahe sarve bhavantaṃ praṇatāḥ sthitāḥ
english: "You are our father, our teacher, our kinsman, and we are your sons — so we all hold you, and stand before you bowed."

sanskrit: adya tad viparītaṃ te vadato 'smāsu dṛśyate yadi śatruṃ tvam ātmānaṃ manyase tat tathāstv iha eṣa te sadṛśaṃ śatroḥ karma bhīmaḥ karomy aham
english: "But this day the contrary of that is seen in you as you speak to us. If you hold yourself our enemy, then so be it here; behold, I, Bhīma, do unto you the deed befitting a foe."

sanskrit: athodbhrāmya gadāṃ bhīmaḥ kāladaṇḍam ivāntakaḥ droṇāyāvasṛjad rājan sa rathād avapupluve
english: Then whirling his mace like Death wielding the rod of Time, Bhīma hurled it at Droṇa, O king; and he leaped down from his car.

sanskrit: sāśvasūtadhvajaṃ yānaṃ droṇasyāpothayat tadā prāmṛdnāc ca bahūn yodhān vāyur vṛkṣān ivaujasā
english: Then it crushed Droṇa's vehicle together with horses, driver, and banner, and ground down many warriors, as the wind grinds trees by its force.

sanskrit: taṃ punaḥ parivavrus te tava putrā rathottamam anyaṃ ca ratham āsthāya droṇaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ
english: Then again your sons surrounded that best of cars; and Droṇa, foremost of strikers, mounting another car —

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahārāja bhīmasenaḥ parākramī agrataḥ syandanānīkaṃ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: Then, O great king, the wrathful and valiant Bhīmasena overwhelmed the chariot-host before him with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare tava putrā mahārathāḥ bhīmaṃ bhīmabalaṃ yuddhe 'yodhayaṃs tu jayaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Being struck down in the battle, your sons, the great car-warriors, fought against Bhīma of terrible strength in the fight, seeking victory.

sanskrit: tato duḥśāsanaḥ kruddho rathaśaktiṃ samākṣipat sarvapāraśavīṃ tīkṣṇāṃ jighāṃsuḥ pāṇḍunandanam
english: Then Duḥśāsana, enraged, hurled a chariot-lance, all of steel and keen, eager to slay the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: āpatantīṃ mahāśaktiṃ tava putrapracoditām dvidhā ciccheda tāṃ bhīmas tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: That great lance flying upon him, sped by your son, Bhīma cleft in two; and that seemed a wondrous thing.

sanskrit: athānyair niśitair bāṇaiḥ saṃkruddhaḥ kuṇḍabhedinam suṣeṇaṃ dīrghanetraṃ ca tribhis trīn avadhīd balī
english: Then, enraged, with other whetted arrows the mighty one slew with three shafts the three — Kuṇḍabhedī, Suṣeṇa, and Dīrghanetra.

sanskrit: tato vṛndārakaṃ vīraṃ kurūṇāṃ kīrtivardhanam putrāṇāṃ tava vīrāṇāṃ yudhyatām avadhīt punaḥ
english: Then he slew again Vṛndāraka, the hero, the increaser of the Kurus' fame, one of your valiant sons as they fought.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ raudrakarmāṇaṃ durvimocanam eva ca tribhis trīn avadhīd bhīmaḥ punar eva sutāṃs tava
english: Abhaya and Raudrakarman, and Durvimocana too — these three sons of yours Bhīma slew again with three shafts.

sanskrit: vadhyamānā mahārāja putrās tava balīyasā bhīmaṃ praharatāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ samantāt paryavārayan
english: Being slain, O great king, by that stronger one, your sons hemmed in on every side Bhīma, the foremost of strikers.
